title: The Same Finding, Twice
scopeNote: This keeps the original's single picture, the null distribution of t with the observed statistic marked, and its run-it-again-on-more-people control. The one-tailed against two-tailed comparison, the extended treatment of why t has heavier tails than the normal, and the conclusion-writing exercise stay in the longer version, and the page says so.
summary: An independent-samples t-test read off one figure: the distribution of t when the two populations are identical, with the observed statistic marked and the two-tailed area shaded. Adding people moves t and p a long way and leaves Cohen's d exactly where it was.
learningObjectives: Build t from a mean difference and a standard error and place it on the null distribution.
Read a two-tailed p as the area beyond the observed statistic.
Explain why p depends strongly on the sample size while Cohen's d does not.
Explain what the null distribution is a distribution of, which is not scores or people.
Write a conclusion that says fail to reject rather than accept, and that reports an interval alongside the decision.
interactionTypes: three live controls over the study
a real t-test computed from the summary statistics on screen
the null distribution of t with both tails shaded and the critical values marked
the standard normal drawn behind for comparison
a run-it-again control that repeats the identical finding at a larger sample size
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted. Everything is computed in the browser and is gone when the page is closed.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with every control a native range input carrying a live value output. The figure description gives the degrees of freedom, the critical values, the observed t, the two-tailed p, the standard error and Cohen's d, so no conclusion depends on reading the curve. The observed statistic and the critical values differ by line weight and dash pattern as well as by colour, and both are labelled on the figure. A full written conclusion is generated in text beneath the figures, including the fail-to-reject wording and the interval. The figure scrolls sideways rather than shrinking below legible label sizes on a narrow screen. Changes are announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Illustrative. There is no dataset and no sampling: the inputs are summary statistics the learner sets, and the curve is a Student's t density. No figure is a real result.
simulationNotes: No randomness and nothing to seed. The standard error of the difference is the common spread times the square root of two over n, t is the difference over that standard error on 2n minus 2 degrees of freedom, and the two-tailed p comes from the incomplete beta function. The 95 per cent interval uses a t critical value found by bisection on the same tail function. Cohen's d is shown as a fourth tile specifically so it can be watched sitting still while t and p move, which is the distinction this activity and the overlap activity next door exist to draw between them. Note that the shared statistics module's two-tailed t function is named tTwoTailedP in full, because a shorter name invites a caller to double an already two-tailed probability.
readmeTopic: what a t-test actually asks, and why the sample size changes the answer without changing the finding
